input: list1 and list2 are each null or a list head. The two node sets are disjoint and each input is sorted by nondecreasing val; shared input tails or heads are excluded. Each nonempty input is a finite, acyclic singly linked list of caller-supplied nodes with ordinary data fields val and next. val contains JavaScript Number integers, excluding BigInt; next is another node or null. next fields are writable and nodes within a list are distinct. Accessors, proxies, custom attribute behavior, concurrent observation or mutation during the call, and malformed links are outside the domain. Inputs must fit both runtimes. External caller references to individual nodes are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: The head of the nondecreasing merge, containing every original input node exactly once. Relative order within each input is preserved, and nodes from list1 precede nodes from list2 when values tie. Both empty inputs return null. A sole nonempty input returns its original head.
mutation_aliasing: Relinks only original input nodes through their next fields; values and all other fields are unchanged. No input node is cloned, dropped or replaced. Every original node appears exactly once in the acyclic output, whose tail next is null. The two input lists must be disjoint: shared heads, shared tails and other cross-list node aliases are outside the domain. Other caller-held references to individual nodes remain valid and observe the new next graph; the caller's head reference bindings themselves are not reassigned. One local sentinel is allocated but is never returned or linked from any input node. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The paired domain restricts node values to exact integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], excluding booleans, negative zero, NaN, infinities and BigInt. Python uses plain int and JavaScript uses Number. Values are compared only, never modified or used in arithmetic, so Python and JavaScript comparisons agree on this domain. No list-length counter, bitwise coercion or recursion depth is used.
complexity: O(n + m + 1) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space for input lengths n and m. Each merge-loop iteration advances exactly one input cursor; the remaining suffix is attached in O(1) time. One sentinel and a constant number of borrowed references are charged. No recursion, node copies, arrays, sorting or value arithmetic is used. Field access, reference assignment and bounded-integer comparisons are constant cost.

helpers.name: Link
helpers.contract: A local sentinel-only class whose constructor stores the supplied next_node reference, defaulting to null, in its sole instance data field next. It does not read, copy or construct caller ListNode objects and has no val field. Sentinels never become nodes in the returned list.
helpers.cost: One constructor call allocates one sentinel object, each in O(1) time and O(1) space. The complete 80-byte UTF-8 helper definition, from class Link through its final definition newline, is byte-identical in 0021.js, 0024.js and 0086.js, and is fully charged in every standalone candidate. Separator newlines are charged in total source bytes.

source_accounting: The complete standalone candidate is 628 UTF-8 bytes, including the 80-byte Link helper, input-shape comment, separator newlines, Solution wrapper, method, constructor calls and terminal newline. Caller ListNode is an explicit input shape, not an uncharged dummy-node constructor: all allocated sentinels use the fully included Link implementation. Shared helper spelling is not a free library. There are no imports, generated source or hidden expansion. Any eventual judge adapter is additional charged source.
evidence_boundary: Independently authored dev_fit candidate outside frozen source sets. No candidate execution, predecessor equivalence, behavioral qualification, benchmark acceptance or M1 progress is claimed. The mandatory isolated judge is unavailable; AST parsing, JavaScript syntax and metadata checks do not establish runtime correctness. Independent source-bound qualification must compare value order, mapped original node identities and the complete post-call next graph, including caller aliases and terminal null links, not just serialized values. Empty, singleton, duplicate-value and odd/even-length inputs plus declared ordering boundaries require qualification before promotion.
